$comment: Evidence package for a viable HSV-2 cure design. Combines: (1) measured outcome distribution from an organoid study, (2) elimination verification via detection vector assay, (3) controls and long-term follow-up.

subject.mechanism: Dual meganuclease excision of HSV-2 genome from latently infected sacral DRG neurons
subject.delivery: AAV9 intrathecal injection to sacral DRG
subject.verification: dCas9-VPR-GFP reporter assay at 28 days post-treatment
subject.model: human DRG organoid (iPSC-derived) latently infected with HSV-2 strain 333
subject.follow_up: 90 days, no viral reactivation in cleared neurons

facts.note: 98% clearance in human DRG organoid model. 24/1200 neurons retained residual HSV DNA at day 28. No reactivation observed in cleared neurons through 90-day follow-up. The 2% residual rate is the current ceiling — whether it can be driven lower with repeated dosing is an open question.

subject.specificity: no cross-reactivity with human genome (guides return 0 hits)

subject.observation: Cleared neurons subjected to reactivation stimuli (heat stress, UV, dexamethasone) at days 30, 60, 90
subject.result: 0/1176 cleared neurons showed viral gene expression post-stimulus
subject.control: 24/24 residual-positive neurons reactivated under same stimuli
subject.interpretation: Excision is durable. Cleared cells do not harbor reactivation-competent virus.

data.method: Single-cell long-read sequencing of treated neurons at day 28
data.note: 91% deletion (HSV genome region between guides removed). 2.5% indel (guides hit but repair preserved some viral sequence — these cells showed no viral gene expression). 2% uncut (delivery failure, not resistance). Rejoined (1%) and inverted (0.5%) are named and counted. Total functional cure rate: deleted + degraded + indel = 96%.
